label: last two copy-phase outputs (end of copy), length-dependent
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original input or at <DEL>), and only on repeated-input steps (in_first=0). It is concentrated on the final two copy steps (to_go 0 or 1 holds ~89% of activation mass, to_go<=2 ~96%). How reliably it fires there depends on sequence length: always for L=3 (both steps, including the strongest activations ~0.09, peaking on the final step of 3-token sequences), often for L=4, 6, 7, rarely for L=5 and L=8, while for L=8-9 it spreads earlier (to_go 2-3). Within those steps it shows a weak preference for some input tokens (h, o, 2), but token identity does not explain which steps fire. Outside the end of the copy phase it is nearly silent. Simple predicate (phase==2)&(to_go<=1) gives dev recall 0.82 / mass 0.89 but precision 0.26; restricting to L in {3,4,6,7} gives F1 ~0.51.
